findings.title: One MTA Employee Exercised Excessive Control Over Certain Interagency Agreements Which Circumvented State Procurement Regulations and Allowed MTA to Augment its Staff Beyond its Budgetary Positions
findings.description: MTA lacked adequate controls over interagency agreements with Towson University's Division of Economic and Community Outreach (DECO). One employee had unilateral authority, agreements circumvented procurement regulations by using private vendors without competitive bids, and individuals were not independently hired by DECO. Estimated administrative fees totaled $629,324.

dollar_amounts.context: subcontractor invoices accounted for
estimated administrative fees during fiscal years 2010 through 2013

findings.recommendation: Ensure that the agreements and related amendments and task orders are subject to independent supervisory review and approval; discontinue its practice of using interagency agreements to circumvent budgetary restrictions and procurement regulations.

findings.title: The Cost of Certain Services Appeared Excessive or Varied Among Similar Services, and the Related Terms Precluded Effective Monitoring of Hours Worked
findings.description: Amounts paid for certain services appeared excessive or varied among similar services. The employment services agreement specified salaries but not hours worked, precluding effective monitoring. MTA could not explain how pricing was developed.

fee in the fiscal year 2013 agreement
fee paid for one individual more than another with same job description

findings.recommendation: Ensure amounts paid under interagency agreements are reasonable and supported; ensure agreements contain sufficient details to enable effective monitoring.

findings.title: Advanced Payment and Lack of Documentation Precluded Effective Verification of Amounts Billed and Certain Charges Were Inconsistent with or Were Not Authorized in the Related Task Order. Records of the Agreements, Amendments, and Related Task Orders Were Not Maintained
findings.description: MTA made advance payments without verifying services were provided. Invoices lacked support for amounts billed, and charges were inconsistent with task orders. MTA could not provide a comprehensive listing of agreements or copies of numerous documents.

dollar_amounts.context: July 2011 quarterly billing for services to be provided
May 2011 invoice for facility fees without supporting invoice
charges on one invoice for development and delivery of a retreat
fee provided in the related task order for full-day training session
billed per course for facility rental fees
rental fee provided in the related task order per course

findings.recommendation: Only process payments after the related goods and services are received; ensure adequate documentation is obtained to enable verification of amounts invoiced; ensure billings are consistent with amounts and services specified in related task orders; ensure copies of all executed interagency agreements and task orders are on file.

findings.title: MTA Could Not Document That Certain Deliverables Were Received
findings.description: MTA could not document work performed by five individuals for which $571,340 was paid. No documentation provided for charges on six invoices totaling $90,962. Reports indicated some courses were cancelled or attended by only one employee.

invoice total for which MTA provided partial documentation

findings.recommendation: Ensure all deliverables are received prior to making related payments; determine whether the aforementioned deliverables were obtained and take appropriate corrective action, including recovery of funds.

findings.title: MTA Did Not Take Adequate Follow-up Action When Questionable Activities of One Employee Were Identified
findings.description: MTA did not refer the matter to the Office of the Attorney General's Criminal Division initially and did not conduct a thorough review of agreements despite identified control deficiencies. The employee had unilateral control, and there were questionable transactions involving the spouse's company.

findings.recommendation: After consultation with the Attorney General, review transactions and recover any amounts determined to be improperly billed; conduct a thorough review of agreements and all related payments and take appropriate follow-up action; notify the Governor's Chief Legal Counsel.

extraction.agency_response_summary: MTA concurs with all recommendations and notes implementation of new Standard Operating Procedures effective December 1, 2014, requiring additional scrutiny and approval for interagency agreements. They are conducting evaluations to determine if deliverables were obtained and will take corrective action by July 31, 2015.
extraction.extraction_notes: Report date derived from cover page 'February 2015'. Audit period covers fiscal years 2010 through 2013. Criminal referral confirmed by text stating matters were referred to the Criminal Division of the Office of Attorney General in May 2013.
